{{Short description|French mathematician}}
[[File:Georges Reeb, Paul Vincensini, Charles Ehresmann.jpeg|300px|thumb|''Left to right:'' [[Georges Reeb]], Paul Vincensini, and [[Charles Ehresmann]], at a topology conference in [[Mathematical Research Institute of Oberwolfach|Oberwolfach]], 1949]]
'''Paul Félix Vincensini''' (30 April 1896, in [[Bastia]] – 9 August 1978, in [[La Ciotat]])<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://oda.mfo.de/downloads/frei/bsz324780621/1/bsz324780621_abstract.pdf |title=Oberwolfach Guest Book (April 1946 – August 1954) |access-date=2017-07-04 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304131642/http://oda.mfo.de/downloads/frei/bsz324780621/1/bsz324780621_abstract.pdf |archive-date=2016-03-04 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="montesoro.net">[https://www.montesoro.net/paul.html Paul Vincensini (1896 / 1978)]</ref>
was a French mathematician.

In 1927, he wrote his dissertation ''Sur trois types de congruences rectilignes'' at the [[University of Toulouse]].<ref>[http://data.bnf.fr/12367972/paul_vincensini Record] at data.bnf.fr</ref><ref>[http://bibliotheques.mnhn.fr/medias/detailstatic.aspx?INSTANCE=exploitation&RSC_BASE=HORIZON&RSC_DOCID=227896 Record] at bibliotheques.mnhn.fr</ref><ref>{{cite thesis | type=Ph.D. thesis | url=http://www.numdam.org/article/AFST_1927_3_19__93_0.pdf | author=Paul Félix Vincensini | title=Sur trois types de congruences rectilignes | institution=University of Toulouse | year=1927 }}</ref>
In 1945, working as a Professor at the [[University of Besançon]], he was awarded the [[Charles Dupin]] Prize of the [[French Academy of Sciences]], for his work in higher geometry.<ref>[https://projecteuclid.org/download/pdf_1/euclid.bams/1183507918 Bulletin] of the AMS (May 1946, Notes, p.408)</ref>
In 1949, he got the Prix de la Pensée Française. 
In the same year, he went to Marseille University.
He retired in 1967, but still accepted presidency of a symposium of the Florence Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematical Sciences in 1978.<ref name="montesoro.net"/>
